κεῖμαι.long: I lie, recline, am placed, am laid, set, specially appointed, destined.
κεῖμαι.kj: be (appointed, laid up, made, set), lay, lie
κεῖμαι.der: middle voice of a primary verb;
κεῖμαι.as:
κεῖμαι,
[in LXX: Je 24:1 (יעד hoph.), al.;]
used as passive of τίθημι (LS, s.v.), to be laid, to lie;
(a) of persons: an infant, Lk 2:12, 16; a dead body, Mt 28:6, Lk 23:53, Jo 20:12;
(b) of things, to lie, be laid or set, stand: Mt 5:14, Jo 2:619:2920:5-721:9, Re 4:221:16; trop., Θεμέλιος, I Co 3:11; seq. prep. c. acc., πρός, Mt 3:10, Lk 3:9; εἰς, Lk 12:19; ἐπί, trop., κάλυμμα, II Co 3:15. Metaph., ὁ κόσμος ἐν τ. πονηριῷ κ., I Jo 5:19; to be laid down, appointed: of law, c. dat. pers., I Ti 1:9; seq. εἰς c. acc. (of purpose), Lk 2:34, Phl 1:16, I Th 3:3 (cf. ἀνά-, συν-ανά-, ἀντί-, ἀπό-, ἐπί-, κατά-, παρά-, περί-, πρό-κειμαι).†

κεραία.long: a little hook, an apostrophe on letters of the alphabet, distinguishing them from other little letters, or a separation stroke between letters.
κεραία.sd: something horn-like, i.e. (specially) the apex of a Hebrew letter (figuratively, the least particle)
κεραία.der: feminine of a presumed derivative of the base of G2768 (κέρας);
κεραία.as:
* κεραία (WH, κερέα, v. App., 151), -ας, ἡ
(< κέρας),
a little horn: of the point or extremity which distinguishes some Heb. letters from others (e.g. ד from ר; DCG, ii, 733), Mt 5:18, Lk 16:17.†

κεφαλή.long: (a) the head, (b) met: a corner stone, uniting two walls; head, ruler, lord.
κεφαλή.sd: the head (as the part most readily taken hold of), literally or figuratively
κεφαλή.der: from the primary (in the sense of seizing);
κεφαλή.as:
κεφαλή, -ῆς, ἡ,
[in LXX nearly always for רֹאשׁ;]
the head: Mt 5:36, Mk 6:24, Re 1:149:7, al. mult.; fig., ἄνθρακες ἐπὶ τὴν κ., Ro 12:20(LXX); αἷμα, Ac 18:6; metaph., of a husband, c. gen., I Co 11:3, Eph 5:23; of Christ, I Co 11:3, Eph 4:155:23, Col 1:182:10, 19; of things, κ. γωνίας, Mt 21:42(LXX).

κελεύω.sd: "hail"; to incite by word, i.e. order
κελεύω.as:
** κελεύω,
[in LXX: I Es 9:53, To 8:18, al., and freq. in I-IV Mac;]
to urge on, bid by word of mouth, order, command (mostly of one in authority): c. acc. et. inf. aor., Mt 14:19, 2818:2527:64, Lk 18:40, Ac 4:155:348:3822:3023:1025:6, 17; with ellipse of acc., Mt 8:1814:927:58, Ac 12:1921:33; c. acc. et. inf. Pres., Ac 21:3422:2423:3, 3525:2127:43; with ellipse of acc., Ac 16:22; ptcp. aor., Ac 25:23.†
SYN.: v.s. ἐντέλλω.

κερδαίνω.long: I gain, acquire, win (over), avoid loss.
κερδαίνω.as:
** κερδαίνω,
[in Sm.: Jb 22:3*;]
to gain: c. acc., Mt 25:16, 17, 20, 22; τ. κόσμον, Mt 16:26, Mk 8:36, Lk 9:25; absol., to make profit, get gain: Ja 4:13. Metaph., c. acc. rei, to save oneself from, avoid: Ac 27:21 (Field, Notes, 145); c. acc. pers., to gain, win: Mt 18:15, I Co 9:19-22, Phl 3:8; pass., I Pe 3:1.†

κεραμεύς.as:
κεραμεύς, -εως, ὁ
(< κεράννυμι), [in LXX for יצר, Ps 2:9, Je 18:2, al.;]
a potter: Ro 9:21; ὁ ἀγρὸς τοῦ κ., Mt 27:7, 10(LXX).†

κενός.long: (a) empty, (b) met: empty (in moral content), vain, ineffective, foolish, worthless, (c) false, unreal, pretentious, hollow.
κενός.as:
κενός, -ή, -όν,
[in LXX chiefly for ריק and cognate forms;]
empty (Ge 37:24, Jg 7:16). Metaph.,
(a)empty, vain: λόγοι, Eph 5:6; ἀπάτη, Col 2:8; κήρυγμα, πίστις, I Co 15:14;
(b)vain, fruitless: ἡ χάρις, I Co 15:10; κόπος, I Co 15:58; ἡ εἴσοδος, I Th 2:1; κενά, Ac 4:25(LXX); εἰς κενόν, in vain, to no purpose (Diod., LXX; cl. διὰ κενῆς), II Co 6:1, Ga 2:2, Phl 2:16, I Th 3:5;
(c) of persons, empty-handed: Mk 12:3, Lk 1:5320:10, 11; vain, Ja 2:20.†
SYN.: μάταιος, of the aim or effect of an action, κ. of its quality (Lft. on Cl. Rom., I Co., § 7; Tr., Syn., xlix).

κεφαλιόω.as:
** κεφαλιόω (Rec. -αιόω, [so in LXX: Si 35 (32):8*]), -ῶ
(< κεφάλιον, dimin. of κεφαλή, in late writers);
1. (-αιόω) to sum up (Thuc., al.).
2. (In NT, only) to wound on the head: Mk 12:4.†

κεράμιον.der: neuter of a presumed derivative of G2766 (κέραμος);
κεράμιον.as:
κεράμιον, -ου, τό
(< κέραμος), [in LXX: Je 42 (35):5 (גָּבִיעַ), etc.;]
an earthen vessel, a jar or jug: ὕδατος, Mk 14:13, Lk 22:10.†

κεντυρίων.long: a centurion, an officer commanding about a hundred infantry in the Roman army.
κεντυρίων.sd: a centurion, i.e. captain of one hundred soldiers
κεντυρίων.as:
*† κεντυρίων, -ωνος, ὁ (Lat. centurio);
a centurion: Mk 15:39, 44, 45 (Mt, Lk, use ἑκατόνταρχος (-ης), q.v.).†

κέρας.long: (a) a horn, (b) a horn-like projection at the corner of an altar, (c) a horn as a symbol of power.
κέρας.der: from a primary (the hair of the head);
κέρας.as:
κέρας, -ατος
(pl. not irreg. as in Attic), τό, [in LXX chiefly for קֶרֶן;]
a horn: Re 5:612:313:1, 1117:3, 7, 12, 16; of the projections at the corners of the altar (Ex 29:12, al.): Re 9:13. Metaph., as symbol of strength, κ. σωτηρίας (cf. Ps 17 (18):3, al.): Lk 1:69.†

κέραμος.sd: earthenware, i.e. a tile (by analogy, a thin roof or awning)
κέραμος.der: probably from the base of G2767 (κεράννυμι) (through the idea of mixing clay and water);
κέραμος.as:
κεραμος, -ου, ὁ
(< κεράννυμι), [in LXX: II Ki 17:28 (יוֹצֵרכְּלִי)*;]
1.potter's clay.
2.an earthen vessel.
3.a tile: Lk 5:19.†

κεράτιον.sd: something horned, i.e. (specially) the pod of the carob-tree
κεράτιον.der: neuter of a presumed derivative of G2768 (κέρας);
κεράτιον.as:
* κεράτιον, -ου, τό
(dimin. of κέρας),
1.a little horn (Arist.).
2. In pl. (the fruit of the κερατέα), carob-pods: Lk 15:16.†

κερματιστής.long: properly: a changer of large into smaller coins, a money-changer.
κερματιστής.sd: a handler of coins, i.e. money-broker
κερματιστής.as:
*† κερματιστής, -οῦ, ὁ
(κερματίζω, to cut small, coin into small money),
a money changer: Jo 2:14.†

κέρμα.long: a small coin; plur: small change.
κέρμα.as:
* κέρμα, -τος, τό
(< κείρω),
1.a slice, hence,
2.a small coin: pl., Jo 2:15.†

κειρία.long: a kind of girdle made of cords; a bandage, grave clothes.
κειρία.as:
κειρία, -ας, ἡ,
[in LXX: Pr 7:16 (מַרְבַּדִּים)*;]
a vernacular word,
1a bed-cord (Aristoph., AV., 816;Pr 7:16.).
2. In pl., swathings (cf. Field, Notes, 96 f.): Jo 11:44.†

Κεδρών.sd: Cedron (i.e. Kidron), a brook near Jerusalem
Κεδρών.as:
Κεδρών
(v.s. κέδρος), ὁ, indecl. (in FlJ, gen. -ῶνος; Heb. קִדְרוֹן), [in LXX: II Ki 15:23, IV Ki 23:6, al.;]
Cedron (OT, Kidron): χείμαρρος τοῦ Κ., Jo 18:1 (L, Tr., mg., R, txt.; cf. Bl., § 10, 5; Lft., Essays, 172 ff).†

κείρω.g: I shear, cut the hair of
κείρω.long: I shear, cut the hair of; mid: I cut my own hair, have my hair cut.
κείρω.as:
κείρω,
[in LXX chiefly for גּזז, Is 53:7, al.;]
to cut short the hair, shear: a sheep, Ac 8:32 (Is 53:7). Mid., to have one's hair cut off, be shorn: absol., I Co 11:6; τ. κεφαλήν, Ac 18:18.†

Κεγχρεαί.long: Cenchreae, the port of Corinth on the Saronic Gulf.

κεφάλαιον.g: the chief matter, a sum of money
κεφάλαιον.long: (a) the chief matter, the main point, (b) a sum of money.
κεφάλαιον.sd: a principal thing, i.e. main point; specially, an amount (of money)
κεφάλαιον.der: neuter of a derivative of G2776 (κεφαλή);
κεφάλαιον.as:
κεφάλαιος, -α, -ον
(< κεφαλή), [in LXX (-αιον, τό) for רֹאשׁ, Nu 4:2, al.;]
of the head; metaph., principal, chief; mostly as subst., κεφάλαιον, τό;
1.the chief point: He 8:1.
2.the sum total, amount: Ac 22:28 (other meaning, LS, s.v.).†

κέντρον.long: a sting, goad; met: of death.
κέντρον.sd: a point ("centre"), i.e. a sting (figuratively, poison) or goad (figuratively, divine impulse)
κέντρον.as:
κέντρον, -ου, τό
(< κεντέω, to prick), [in LXX: Pr 26:3 (מֶתֶג), Ho 13:14 (קֹטֶב), 5:12, Si 38:25, IV Mac 14:19*;]
1.a sting (IV Mac 14:19): Re 9:10. Metaph. (as Ho 13:14): τ. θανάτου, I Co 15:55(LXX), 56.
2.a goad: pl., Ac 26:14.†

κενόω.g: I empty, deprive of content, make unreal
κενόω.long: (a) I empty, (b) I deprive of content, make unreal.
κενόω.sd: to make empty, i.e. (figuratively) to abase, neutralize, falsify
κενόω.kj: make (of none effect, of no reputation, void), be in vain
κενόω.as:
κενόω, -ῶ
(< κενός, q.v.), [in LXX: Je 14:215:9 (אמל pu.)*;]
to empty. Metaph., to empty, make empty, vain or of no effect: καύχημα, I Co 9:15; ἑαυτόν, of Christ, Phl 2:7 (v Lft.; ICC, in l, and esp. Gifford, Incarn., 54 ff.); pass., πίστις, Ro 4:14; ὁ σταυρός, I Co 1:17; καύχημα, II Co 9:3.†

κέρδος.as:
** κέρδος, -εος (-ους), τό,
[in Aq.: Ez 27:24; Sm.: Ps 29 (30):10, al.;]
gain: Phl 1:213:7, Tit 1:11.†

κενοδοξία.as:
**† κενοδοξία, -ας, ἡ
(< κενόδοξος), [in LXX: Wi 14:14, II Mac 2:158:19*;]
1.foolish fancy, vain opinion, error (LXX, Wi 14:14, II Mac 2:158:19).
2.vainglory, groundless conceit: Phl 2:3.†

κέλευσμα.g: a word of command, a call
κέλευσμα.long: a word of command, a call, an arousing outcry.
κέλευσμα.as:
κέλευσμα, -τος, τό,
(< κελεύω), [in LXX: Pr 24:62 (30:27)*;]
a call, summons, shout of command: I Th 4:16 (v. M, Th., in l.).†

κενοφωνία.der: from a presumed compound of G2756 (κενός) and G5456 (φωνή);
κενοφωνία.as:
*† κενοφωνία, -ας, ἡ
(< κενός, φωνέω), [cf. κενολογέω (צפף), Is 8:19*;]
empty talk, babbling: pl., I Ti 6:20, II Ti 2:16.†

κεφαλίς.long: (lit: little head, then: the knob at the end of the wooden core of a roll of papyrus, then) a roll, volume, division (of a book).
κεφαλίς.sd: properly, a knob, i.e. (by implication) a roll (by extension from the end of a stick on which the manuscript was rolled)
κεφαλίς.as:
κεφαλίς, -ίδος, ἡ
(dimin. of κεφαλή), [in LXX for מְגִלָּה, וָו, etc.;]
1.a little head.
2.an extremity, capital (of a column).
3. (As in Ez 2:9, Ps 39 (40):8, II Es 6:2) a roll: κ. βιβλίου, He 10:7(LXX).†

κενῶς.long: falsely, in vain, to no purpose.
κενῶς.as:
κενῶς,
adv.,
[in LXX: Is 49:4 (לְרִיק)*;]
in vain, to no purpose: Ja 4:5.†

κεραμικός.g: of clay, made by a potter
κεραμικός.long: of clay, made by a potter, earthen.
κεραμικός.as:
κεραμικός, -ή, -όν
(< κέραμος), [in LXX: Da LXX 2:41 (פֶּחָר)*;]
1. (cl.) of a potter (e.g. γῆ).
2. In LXX and NT, = cl., κεραμεοῦς (Plut., κεράμειος, Polyb., -μαῖος, etc), earthen: Re 2:27.†

κεράννυμι.g: I mix, pour out for drinking
κεράννυμι.long: I mix, mingle, pour out for drinking.
κεράννυμι.sd: to mingle, i.e. (by implication) to pour out (for drinking)
κεράννυμι.der: prolonged form of a more primary (which is used in certain tenses);
κεράννυμι.as:
κεράννυμι,
[in LXX for מסךְ, Is 5:22, al.;]
to mix, mingle, chiefly of the diluting of wine: Re 18:6; by oxymoron, κεκεράσμενος ἄκρατος, Re 14:10.†
SYN.: μίγνυμι. κ. implies "a mixing of two things, so that they are blended and form a compound, as in wine and water, whereas μ. implies a mixing without such composition, as in two sorts of grain" (LS, s.v. κρᾶσις).
